artifacts.summary: 3-phase plan adopting heredoc-aware stripping in validate-bounded-waiter.sh: conservative awk body-stripper plus header ruling and 8 new fixtures, a bail-path Write/Edit refusal hint, then redeploy and full gate.

memory_candidates.content: A PreToolUse hook registered with matcher "Bash" that detects a forbidden shape by pattern-matching the raw tool_input.command string cannot distinguish a heredoc BODY (inert data being written to a file) from live shell control flow, because tool_input.command preserves the literal multi-line script text. The consequence is self-reinforcing: documentation ABOUT the forbidden shape is exactly the content class the detector refuses, so the obstruction recurs every time the rule is extended or restated. Hooks matching Write|Edit never face this, since their payload is already the complete target content rather than a shell command containing an embedded sub-document -- which is why a hook family can accumulate several textual-shape hooks with no heredoc handling anywhere. The safe fix shape is a conservative region-stripper (blank heredoc body lines, then apply the unchanged detection conjunction to what remains) that bails to the unstripped text on anything it cannot parse confidently, so ambiguity never resolves toward allowing. Narrowing the detector to require the keyword in command position does NOT fix it: a quoted shell example genuinely sits in command position inside the body.
